missionPremise: G-146's row body (OPS-17) names exactly two remaining defects in the design declarations: (1) `_design/all-canvas/build.mjs` declares 72 boards across 17 surfaces while three 2026-09-18 designs exist on disk and are declared nowhere on it, and (2) the vocabulary defect in `_design/plan-review/gen.mjs` is translated at build time by the review-artefact build script rather than fixed at source. Source: OPS-17 row G-146 plus amendment A-152 ('the all-canvas omission ... has MOVED to three others'; 'the vocabulary loose end is NOT closed and is UNMEASURED from this seat').
completionPredicate: The canvas declares every design folder that exists on disk, so the operator can reach the People and access DRAFT they are being asked to ratify; and `_design/plan-review/gen.mjs` emits the customer-facing citation and trace wording itself, so the wrong strings no longer survive in the source for a consumer who does not run `_design/bastrop-review/build.mjs`. NOT reachable in this lane: `design-completion-gate.mjs` exit 0, because the four R3 findings belong to G-164.
scopeBasis: Write set is the dispatch's four files (`_design/all-canvas/build.mjs`, `_design/plan-review/gen.mjs`, `_design/INDEX.md`, `_design/surface_coverage.json`). The four `_design/` folders owned by the sibling lane g164-design-repairs were not opened, read or written. `_design/plan-review/*` board files are written ONLY by running the in-scope `gen.mjs`, and `_design/all-canvas/*` derived files ONLY by running the in-scope `build.mjs`; no out-of-scope file was edited.

rootDecision.why: The dispatch fixes the lane's artifact root to 'the doc_repo worktree the session RUNNING YOU is rooted in' and forbids P:/doc_repo as the integration seat's checkout. Two candidate roots were measured and both rejected on evidence rather than preference. (a) P:/seat-worktrees/dispatch-planner/doc_repo, the seat worktree where this queue's sibling lanes (g150, g152, g153, g155, g156) filed, is at `seat/dispatch-planner` 07d45d3a, **149 commits behind main**, and its `_design/` does not contain smartcity-citizen-lens, smartcity-people-and-access or smartcity-records-search at all — the mission's two residues cannot be reproduced there. (b) P:/doc_repo was excluded by the dispatch. It also carries 20 modified and 104 untracked paths belonging to the integration seat. A fresh worktree from main was therefore cut so the mission's inputs exist and no other seat's working tree is touched (AGENT_CONTRACT section 5: work in an isolated worktree).
rootDecision.conventionDeviation: Recorded so the planner can find the artifacts. The sibling g153 lane's close states the practice for this queue is to file artifacts in the dispatch planner's seat worktree. That practice is not followable here, for the reason above, so this lane's artifacts are in its own worktree and are named by pathspec in the close. No claim and no artifact was written into P:/doc_repo or into the dispatch planner's worktree.

Both predicates independently reproduce the same 20 and the same 3, and the row's wider predicate (26 subdirs less the 6 named non-design dirs) also yields exactly 20, so the two are not two ways of saying one thing by construction.

RE_DERIVED_1_declarationComparison.verdict: The row's claim HOLDS. The undeclared set is exactly the three it names, on both predicates. A different set was pre-registered as the expected outcome of a failure and did not occur.

boardsAndSurfacesRecounted.note: My first instrument counted `.dc.html` across the whole file and read 76. Four occurrences live outside the ROWS table (`stem + '.dc.html'` twice in the writer, `'main.dc.html'` in the entry-artboard assertion, and `.replace('.dc.html','')` in the log line). Scoped to the ROWS literal it reads 72, which matches the row. The 76 was my instrument's defect, not a second declaration: the two numbers that should agree now do, and the reconciliation is recorded rather than rounded off (DEV-PROCESS 1.4).

RE_DERIVED_1_declarationComparison.corroborationThatIndexAndCoverageAreAlre: The gate's R1, R2 and R4 are all ZERO on the baseline run, so `_design/INDEX.md` and `_design/surface_coverage.json` already agree with both the filesystem and the shipped nav. `surface_coverage.json` already maps `citizen` -> smartcity-citizen-lens, `records` -> smartcity-records-search and `people` -> smartcity-people-and-access (planRow G-143). Adding those three to surface_coverage.json would actively BREAK R4, which refuses a declared surface the product does not ship, and all three are DRAFTs outside the shipped nav. So `surface_coverage.json` is expected to need NO change, and that expectation is falsifiable: if R4 goes non-zero after my edits, I was wrong.

RE_DERIVED_2_vocabulary.correctionToThePlanner: A-152 states that 'the review-artefact build script's home is not in `doc_repo`, so the write path cannot be read from here'. That is FALSE and it is the reason this dispatch's write list is one file short. The review-artefact build script is `_design/bastrop-review/build.mjs`, it is in doc_repo, it is tracked, and it contains the translation verbatim at lines 28-33. Reported per DEV-PROCESS 3.2; not acted on, per the dispatch's own instruction to stop rather than widen the write set.
RE_DERIVED_2_vocabulary.fixChosen: Make `_design/plan-review/gen.mjs` emit exactly what the customer document already renders, so the published artifact is behaviour-preserving and the source no longer carries the defect: the QA note is removed (the translation removed it, so the document showed nothing), and the four citation/trace strings take the translated wording. Then the translations match nothing and are inert.
RE_DERIVED_2_vocabulary.consequentialWrites: Running the in-scope `gen.mjs` rewrites `_design/plan-review/{Main,Review,Embedded}.dc.html` and `canvas.json`. Those are the generator's own outputs; a fix that left them un-regenerated would leave the defect visible on the boards, which is the thing the mission says must not survive. Declared here rather than presented as four edited files.

baselineGate.significantStructuralFinding: The gate does NOT read `_design/all-canvas/build.mjs`. Its declaration inputs are INDEX.md and surface_coverage.json only, and both already agree with the filesystem. So the canvas declaration is a FOURTH declaration surface that no control watches, and fixing it cannot move the gate's output. That is exactly why the omission stayed invisible for three days, and it is why the gate will read identically before and after except for the R3 lines g164 owns. Pre-registered so an unchanged after-run is not mistaken for a failed fix.
